What is the worst part about having to wear glasses/contacts? Would you consider LASIK (laser eye surgery)?

I'm very nearsighted and have worn glasses since I was 5 (I'm 45 now). I wore contacts from age 16 to 35, though by the time I was in my late 20s I only wore them to go out to clubs or whatever, the rest of the time I always wore glasses.

Glasses: frequently get dust and fingerprints on them, steam up when you go outside after having been in air conditioning, fall off the damn nightstand whenever you reach for them, and make things smaller than they are in real life.

Contacts: dry out in air conditioning, dry out when you stare at a computer screen too long because they make you blink less, dry out when you've had too much to drink, dry out when you sleep with them on. You have to clean them which is a hassle. And god forbid you should get a hair or something trapped behind one.

Unfortunately, I am a poor candidate for laser eye surgery. With my prescription, I would have to live with too many tradeoffs, like having one eye more farsighted and one eye more nearsighted. I don't want to deal with any of that. Glasses are inconvenient but there are no health issues associated with them.
Been wearing glasses for over 20 years and I love them. I tried contacts for a while by was annoyed by how many times I had to use rewetting drops. Bottom line: do what is right for you.
Got LASIK a few years ago. Best decision ever.
rain is the worst part of glasses!

If you ever woke up and could not find your glasses then you know what its like. I can not see without my glasses. There have been many times they broke, fell off at inconvenient times or places, or like I said, woke up and can not find them. I have been wearing them for 52 years. They are like a millstone around my neck. I once got some metal fragments in my eye and had to have them removed, the next day when the bandage was removed I could see perfect from that eye. It only lasted one day but it was like I was in paradise. If I could afford the LASIK I would jump on it.

I got LASIK five days ago. It's been amazing. Expensive, but definitely worth it if you can spare the cash and fit the risk profile.

The best part is waking up and immediately being able to see, and going to bed without having to take out my contacts.

Had LASIK surgery about 14 months ago i believe. Wore glasses for 21 years. Greatest decision of my life. Not gonna lie to you the procedure is fucking terrifying. Not painful but just scary as hell. But I have not had a problem with my vision yet. Right after i got it done i had trouble driving at night due to the halos. But that went away pretty pretty quick. I would do it again in a heartbeat if my vision degrades
